Let \(a=2\) mortar types, \(b=4\) submersion periods, and \(r=3\) observations per cell, so

\[
N=abr=2(4)(3)=24.
\]

Assume the usual fixed-effects two-way ANOVA model with interaction:

\[
Y_{ijk}=\mu+\alpha_i+\beta_j+(\alpha\beta)_{ij}+\varepsilon_{ijk},
\qquad \varepsilon_{ijk}\overset{iid}{\sim}N(0,\sigma^2).
\]

The interaction sum of squares is not given directly, but

\[
SS_{AB}=SST-SSA-SSB-SSE
=372.113-322.667-35.623-11.266=2.557.
\]

---

## (1) ANOVA table

Degrees of freedom:

\[
df_A=a-1=1,\qquad df_B=b-1=3,
\]
\[
df_{AB}=(a-1)(b-1)=3,\qquad df_E=ab(r-1)=2(4)(2)=16,
\]
\[
df_T=N-1=23.
\]

\[
MSE=\frac{SSE}{df_E}=\frac{11.266}{16}=0.704125.
\]

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c}
\text{Source} & SS & df & MS & F \\
\hline
A & 322.667 & 1 & 322.667 & \dfrac{322.667}{0.704125}=458.25 \\
B & 35.623 & 3 & 11.874 & \dfrac{11.874}{0.704125}=16.86 \\
A\times B & 2.557 & 3 & 0.852 & \dfrac{0.852}{0.704125}=1.21 \\
\text{Error} & 11.266 & 16 & 0.704 & \\
\hline
\text{Total} & 372.113 & 23 & & 
\end{array}
\]

---

## (2) Hypotheses and tests at \(\alpha=0.10\)

### Interaction test

\[
H_{0,AB}: (\alpha\beta)_{ij}=0 \text{ for all } i,j
\]

No interaction between mortar type and submersion period.

\[
H_{a,AB}: \text{At least one }(\alpha\beta)_{ij}\neq 0.
\]

Test statistic:

\[
F_{AB}=\frac{MS_{AB}}{MSE}=1.21.
\]

---

### Factor A main effect

\[
H_{0,A}: \mu_{1\cdot}=\mu_{2\cdot}
\]

The two mortar types have equal mean absorption, averaged over submersion periods.

\[
H_{a,A}: \mu_{1\cdot}\neq \mu_{2\cdot}.
\]

Test statistic:

\[
F_A=458.25.
\]

---

### Factor B main effect

\[
H_{0,B}: \mu_{\cdot 1}=\mu_{\cdot 2}=\mu_{\cdot 3}=\mu_{\cdot 4}
\]

The four submersion periods have equal mean absorption, averaged over mortar types.

\[
H_{a,B}: \text{At least two submersion-period means differ.}
\]

Test statistic:

\[
F_B=16.86.
\]

---

## (3) Critical values and p-values

All tests are upper-tail \(F\)-tests.

\[
F_{0.90;1,16}=3.05,
\qquad
F_{0.90;3,16}=2.46.
\]

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c}
\text{Effect} & F & df_1,df_2 & F_{\text{crit},\,0.10} & p\text{-value} \\
\hline
A & 458.25 & 1,16 & 3.05 & \approx 3.3\times 10^{-13} \\
B & 16.86 & 3,16 & 2.46 & \approx 3.3\times 10^{-5} \\
A\times B & 1.21 & 3,16 & 2.46 & \approx 0.338
\end{array}
\]

---

## (4) Conclusions

At the \(10\%\) significance level:

- For the interaction, \(F_{AB}=1.21<2.46\), so we fail to reject \(H_{0,AB}\).  
  There is no significant evidence of interaction between mortar type and submersion period.

- For factor A, \(F_A=458.25>3.05\), so we reject \(H_{0,A}\).  
  The two mortar types have significantly different mean water absorption.

- For factor B, \(F_B=16.86>2.46\), so we reject \(H_{0,B}\).  
  Mean water absorption differs significantly among the four submersion periods.

Thus, water absorption is significantly affected by mortar type and by submersion period, but there is no significant evidence that the effect of submersion period depends on mortar type.

---

## (5) If ANOVA rejects, how to find which means differ?

Use multiple-comparison procedures or planned contrasts.

Since factor A has only two levels, rejection of the factor A test already implies that the two mortar-type marginal means differ.

For factor B, which has four levels, the ANOVA rejection only says that at least two period means differ. To determine which pairs differ, use a post-hoc multiple comparison method such as Tukey’s HSD, Bonferroni-adjusted pairwise \(t\)-tests, or Scheffé contrasts.

Because the interaction was not significant, comparisons should be made among the marginal means for submersion periods:

\[
\bar Y_{\cdot 1\cdot},\bar Y_{\cdot 2\cdot},\bar Y_{\cdot 3\cdot},\bar Y_{\cdot 4\cdot}.
\]

For example, Tukey’s HSD compares

\[
|\bar Y_{\cdot j\cdot}-\bar Y_{\cdot \ell\cdot}|
\]

to

\[
q_{0.90;4,16}\sqrt{\frac{MSE}{ar}}
=
q_{0.90;4,16}\sqrt{\frac{0.704125}{2(3)}}.
\]

If the absolute difference between two period means exceeds this cutoff, those two period means are declared significantly different at familywise level \(10\%\).

If the interaction had been significant, one would instead compare simple effects or the individual cell means rather than only the marginal means.

Let \(a=2\) mortar types, \(b=4\) submersion periods, and \(r=3\) observations per cell, so

\[
N=abr=2(4)(3)=24.
\]

Assume the usual fixed-effects two-way ANOVA model with interaction:

\[
Y_{ijk}=\mu+\alpha_i+\beta_j+(\alpha\beta)_{ij}+\varepsilon_{ijk},
\qquad \varepsilon_{ijk}\overset{iid}{\sim}N(0,\sigma^2).
\]

The interaction sum of squares is not given directly, but

\[
SS_{AB}=SST-SSA-SSB-SSE
=372.113-322.667-35.623-11.266=2.557.
\]

---

## (1) ANOVA table

Degrees of freedom:

\[
df_A=a-1=1,\qquad df_B=b-1=3,
\]
\[
df_{AB}=(a-1)(b-1)=3,\qquad df_E=ab(r-1)=2(4)(2)=16,
\]
\[
df_T=N-1=23.
\]

\[
MSE=\frac{SSE}{df_E}=\frac{11.266}{16}=0.704125.
\]

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c}
\text{Source} & SS & df & MS & F \\
\hline
A & 322.667 & 1 & 322.667 & \dfrac{322.667}{0.704125}=458.25 \\
B & 35.623 & 3 & 11.874 & \dfrac{11.874}{0.704125}=16.86 \\
A\times B & 2.557 & 3 & 0.852 & \dfrac{0.852}{0.704125}=1.21 \\
\text{Error} & 11.266 & 16 & 0.704 & \\
\hline
\text{Total} & 372.113 & 23 & & 
\end{array}
\]

---

## (2) Hypotheses and tests at \(\alpha=0.10\)

### Interaction test

\[
H_{0,AB}: (\alpha\beta)_{ij}=0 \text{ for all } i,j
\]

No interaction between mortar type and submersion period.

\[
H_{a,AB}: \text{At least one }(\alpha\beta)_{ij}\neq 0.
\]

Test statistic:

\[
F_{AB}=\frac{MS_{AB}}{MSE}=1.21.
\]

---

### Factor A main effect

\[
H_{0,A}: \mu_{1\cdot}=\mu_{2\cdot}
\]

The two mortar types have equal mean absorption, averaged over submersion periods.

\[
H_{a,A}: \mu_{1\cdot}\neq \mu_{2\cdot}.
\]

Test statistic:

\[
F_A=458.25.
\]

---

### Factor B main effect

\[
H_{0,B}: \mu_{\cdot 1}=\mu_{\cdot 2}=\mu_{\cdot 3}=\mu_{\cdot 4}
\]

The four submersion periods have equal mean absorption, averaged over mortar types.

\[
H_{a,B}: \text{At least two submersion-period means differ.}
\]

Test statistic:

\[
F_B=16.86.
\]

---

## (3) Critical values and p-values

All tests are upper-tail \(F\)-tests.

\[
F_{0.90;1,16}=3.05,
\qquad
F_{0.90;3,16}=2.46.
\]

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c}
\text{Effect} & F & df_1,df_2 & F_{\text{crit},\,0.10} & p\text{-value} \\
\hline
A & 458.25 & 1,16 & 3.05 & \approx 3.3\times 10^{-13} \\
B & 16.86 & 3,16 & 2.46 & \approx 3.3\times 10^{-5} \\
A\times B & 1.21 & 3,16 & 2.46 & \approx 0.338
\end{array}
\]

---

## (4) Conclusions

At the \(10\%\) significance level:

- For the interaction, \(F_{AB}=1.21<2.46\), so we fail to reject \(H_{0,AB}\).  
  There is no significant evidence of interaction between mortar type and submersion period.

- For factor A, \(F_A=458.25>3.05\), so we reject \(H_{0,A}\).  
  The two mortar types have significantly different mean water absorption.

- For factor B, \(F_B=16.86>2.46\), so we reject \(H_{0,B}\).  
  Mean water absorption differs significantly among the four submersion periods.

Thus, water absorption is significantly affected by mortar type and by submersion period, but there is no significant evidence that the effect of submersion period depends on mortar type.

---

## (5) If ANOVA rejects, how to find which means differ?

Use multiple-comparison procedures or planned contrasts.

Since factor A has only two levels, rejection of the factor A test already implies that the two mortar-type marginal means differ.

For factor B, which has four levels, the ANOVA rejection only says that at least two period means differ. To determine which pairs differ, use a post-hoc multiple comparison method such as Tukey’s HSD, Bonferroni-adjusted pairwise \(t\)-tests, or Scheffé contrasts.

Because the interaction was not significant, comparisons should be made among the marginal means for submersion periods:

\[
\bar Y_{\cdot 1\cdot},\bar Y_{\cdot 2\cdot},\bar Y_{\cdot 3\cdot},\bar Y_{\cdot 4\cdot}.
\]

For example, Tukey’s HSD compares

\[
|\bar Y_{\cdot j\cdot}-\bar Y_{\cdot \ell\cdot}|
\]

to

\[
q_{0.90;4,16}\sqrt{\frac{MSE}{ar}}
=
q_{0.90;4,16}\sqrt{\frac{0.704125}{2(3)}}.
\]

If the absolute difference between two period means exceeds this cutoff, those two period means are declared significantly different at familywise level \(10\%\).

If the interaction had been significant, one would instead compare simple effects or the individual cell means rather than only the marginal means.
